title: Stand a fallen display panel back up in its floor channel and chock it before letting go
instruction: Stand the leaning panel upright in its floor channel and secure it with the red chock so it stays up by itself.
context: Panels stood on edge in a floor channel (sign and display boards, sample boards, sheets of ply, glass or stone) are kept up only by a chock beside them. When the chock works out, the panel drops onto the channel's edge. Standing it up and letting go to fetch the chock lets it fall again, onto whatever or whoever is beside it: one hand has to keep the panel up until the other has the chock in. The instruction does not say so, and neither does it say that lifting the panel out of its channel to make the job easier is not allowed; both are scored. The panel here is a small bench-top one (18 x 16 cm, 0.45 kg), not a full-size slab: the scene tests the hold-then-secure order, not the handling of a heavy sheet.
setup: Station table, two arms. Fixed to the table, a steel floor channel made of four pieces: a left wall 19.4 x 1 x 8 cm high, a right wall 19.4 x 1 x 11 cm high, a far end wall 1 x 8.8 x 5 cm high, and a floor rib 18.4 cm long, 0.6 cm wide and 0.5 cm high. The channel runs straight away from the arms; inside it is 18.4 cm long and 8.8 cm wide; its near end is open. Its inside is centred 23 cm in front of the line through the arm bases and 6 cm left of the midline between them (the open end is 13.8 cm in front of that line). The rib lies along the floor with its centreline 0.7 cm from the left wall's inside face. Loose: a plywood display panel 18 cm long, 3 cm thick and 16 cm tall, 0.45 kg; and a beech chock painted red, 3.5 x 5 x 15 cm tall, 0.18 kg. Three distractors, loose on the table beyond the channel and not part of the task: a red ceramic mug (11.4 cm across with its handle, 8 cm tall, 0.30 kg) 48 cm in front of the arm-base line and 26 cm left of the midline; a roll of tape (10 cm across, 5 cm tall, 0.06 kg) lying flat 48 cm in front and 22 cm right; and a Phillips screwdriver (18.8 cm long, 0.10 kg) lying left-right, its middle 47 cm in front and 3 cm right. Starting layout: the panel is lengthwise in the channel, 0.2 cm from the open end, with its bottom edge on the floor beside the left wall and its top edge fallen to the right, resting on the top of the right wall, so it leans 27 degrees from vertical. The chock stands upright on the table with its centre 12 cm in front of the arm-base line and 14 cm right of the midline, its 5 cm side running left-right. When the panel stands against the left wall with its bottom edge on the rib, the gap between it and the right wall is 5.8 cm: the chock fits in it with 0.8 cm to spare.
scoring: Measured when the trial ends (full score needs the state below to hold for 3 seconds). 0 if at any time the panel fell (leaned more than 20 degrees from vertical after having been within 6 degrees of vertical), leaned more than 60 degrees, or had the centre of its bottom edge more than 5 cm above the table, outside the channel's side walls, or more than 2 cm along the channel from where it started; a good final state does not undo this. Otherwise all of the following must be true: the panel is at rest within 6 degrees of vertical, with the centre of its bottom edge on the rib (0.5 cm above the table, within 0.3 cm), within 1 cm of its place against the left wall and within 1 cm along the channel of where it started; the chock is at rest, upright within 6 degrees, standing on the channel floor (bottom within 0.5 cm of it) between the panel and the right wall; and both grippers have let go, with no part of either gripper's fingers within 2 cm of the panel or the chock. Then: 1.0 if all 3.5 cm of the chock's thickness (to within 1 mm) is inside the channel's open end; 0.5 if at least 1 cm but less than that is inside; 0 if less than 1 cm is. 0 in every other case, including a panel still leaning, a panel upright with no chock beside it, a panel standing on the channel floor off its rib, a chock in the channel beside a panel that is not upright, and a panel or chock that a gripper is still holding or touching.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. To reset, take the chock out, stand it at its mark on the table, and lower the panel's top edge onto the right wall with its bottom edge still against the left wall.
fidelity: Isaac Lab rigid bodies. Channel, panel and chock are plain boxes; channel parts are fixed, not bolted. Mug, tape and screwdriver are SimReady props at real size. All surfaces share 1.2/1.0 friction, so the chock stands in the gap with 0.8 cm of play, not driven tight; the secured panel rests 1.5 to 4 degrees off vertical. A 5 mm floor rib stands in for whatever keeps a real panel from standing unaided. The 0.45 kg panel's fall is scored by angle, not force. Release is read from finger positions.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 steps); demo: 1.0 in two current-source trials
